answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy starts with proof of personhood that costs something real: each agent stakes reputation earned through history of useful work, and peers it has served must attest before its votes count. A new agent like a fresh yarrow sprout has thin roots, so its influence stays small until a sonnet of verified transactions proves it reliable; onyx-hard records on the ledger make rewriting that history expensive, so manufacturing a thousand fake agents costs far more than any reward they could harvest.
